items: Beef fillet, about 1 kg, or about 500 g for a smaller Wellington
250 g chestnut mushrooms, including wild mushrooms if desired
500 g puff pastry, thawed if frozen
2 egg yolks, beaten with 1 teaspoon water
English mustard, for brushing the beef
Optional: chestnuts, for a Christmas-style version

steps: Shape the beef tightly in cling film, then chill so it holds an even shape.
Remove the cling film and quickly sear the beef in a hot pan with a little olive oil for 30 to 60 seconds, until browned all over but still rare in the middle.
Brush the hot beef with mustard, then leave it to cool.
Finely chop the mushrooms. Fry them in a hot pan with olive oil, thyme, salt, and pepper.
Cook the mushrooms over high heat for about 10 minutes, until the moisture has evaporated and the mixture becomes a mushroom paste, or duxelle. Leave to cool.
Roll out the puff pastry on a lightly floured surface into a rectangle large enough to wrap the beef. Chill the pastry.
Lay cling film on the work surface. Arrange the prosciutto or Parma ham in overlapping slices.
Spread the cooled mushroom duxelle over the ham.
Place the cooled beef on top, then use the cling film to roll the ham and mushroom layer tightly around the beef. Chill for at least 30 minutes.
Brush the pastry with egg wash. Remove the cling film from the beef and wrap the pastry around it.
Trim the pastry, seal the edges, then brush all over with egg wash. Chill again for at least 30 minutes.
Score the pastry lightly and brush with egg wash again.
Bake at 200°C / Gas 6 for 15 to 20 minutes, until the pastry is golden and cooked.
Rest for 10 minutes before slicing and serving.
Sources: Gordon Ramsay Beef Wellington method and the existing recipe notes from the page URL.
